title: Regional On-call Rotation Simplification — Retrospective
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

Background: In H2 2025 the platform team expanded regional coverage to three additional cloud regions (eu-west-3, ap-southeast-2, and us-west-3). The on-call rotation grew organically: separate regional rotations, multiple overlap windows, and bespoke escalation rules for legacy services. By late 2025 we observed higher page fatigue, increased cross-region handoffs, and slower mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for multi-region incidents.

This retrospective reviews the simplification project (Project ROTA-SIMP) that ran from 2025-11-02 to 2026-01-28 with the goal to reduce operational cognitive load while preserving SLOs and regional ownership.

Scope and goals:
- Reduce the number of distinct rotations covering core platform services from 6 to 3.
- Reduce cross-region handoffs during incidents by 50% within 2 months of rollout.
- Maintain or improve 99th percentile page-to-acknowledge (P2A) latency.
- Document and publish updated runbooks and dashboard views.

Timeline and milestones:
1. 2025-11-02: Project kickoff; stakeholders: Eng-Platform, Eng-SRE, Eng-Infra, Product.
2. 2025-11-16: Audit of existing rotations and escalation graphs completed.
3. 2025-12-01: Prototype unified regional rotation design approved by oncall leads.
4. 2025-12-15: Small internal pilot with us-central and eu-west on core infra services.
5. 2026-01-05: Gradual rollout to remaining teams and regions.
6. 2026-01-28: Formal project close and start of monitoring phase.

Data and key metrics (pre vs post, baseline window: 2025-09-01 — 2025-11-01; post window: 2026-01-01 — 2026-02-15):
- Number of distinct rotations covering core services: 6 -> 3
- Average page-to-acknowledge (median): 2.4 min -> 2.1 min
- 99th percentile page-to-acknowledge: 18.2 min -> 12.7 min
- Cross-region handoff rate (incidents requiring >1 region team): 34% -> 14%
- Paging noise (pages per oncaller per week): 18 -> 13

Root causes identified:
- Over-specialization: Many rotations were scoped to single-region operational tasks; as services became globally routed, incidents crossed boundaries and required multiple teams.
- Divergent escalation trees: Small, ad-hoc differences in escalation (who to call at 15 vs 20 minutes) created inconsistent behavior.
- Tooling configuration sprawl: Pager and roster configurations lived in multiple spreadsheets and two different PagerDuty teams.
- Insufficient runbook normalization: Runbooks used different naming conventions and inconsistent troubleshooting steps, increasing cognitive load during high-pressure incidents.

What worked well:
- Cross-team working group: Weekly cross-functional syncs (Platform, SRE, Infra) accelerated decisions and surfaced edge cases early.
- Pilot-first rollout: A conservative pilot reduced blast radius and produced real production data.
- Observability changes paired with rota changes: Updating SLO dashboards and adding region labels to alerts made responsibilities clearer.

What didn't work / surprises:
- Short-term increase in duplicate notification noise during reconfiguration windows due to overlapping schedules in PagerDuty. Mitigation required three emergency rollbacks and a follow-up cleanup job.
- Underestimated training time: New oncall run-throughs and handover docs took two additional weeks of SMEs' time.
- A handful of legacy services required custom escalation rules which complicated consolidation.

Decisions made:
- Consolidation model: Adopt a hybrid regional-owner model — three rotations (Americas, EMEA, APAC). Each rotation owns initial triage for services routed to that region; for cross-region stateful failures the owning region coordinates fixes with a designated global follow-up (Global-Fix rotation).
- Standard escalation windows: 0/5/15/30/60 minutes for first/second/tech-lead/engineering-manager/exec escalation respectively for critical SLO breaches.
- Centralized roster storage: Single source of truth in the platform team repo: infra/oncall/roster.yml with automated PagerDuty sync.
- Runbook normalization: All core runbooks must conform to the runbook template (section table below) and include explicit 'handoff' steps.

Runbook template (mandatory fields):
- Service name
- Region labels (Americas/EMEA/APAC/global)
- Owner (primary, secondary)
- Symptoms and first checks (bullet list)
- Quick mitigation steps (ordered)
- Escalation path with contact links and time windows
- Post-incident checklist and RCA pointer

Operational changes to deploy (action items):
- A1: Implement roster.yml and PagerDuty sync automation (owner: Infra-Automation, due 2026-02-15).
- A2: Migrate 42 runbooks to normalized template; prioritize core services (owner: Platform-Docs, due 2026-03-01).
- A3: Update SLO dashboards: add rotation-aware widgets and handoff metrics (owner: Observability, due 2026-02-10).
- A4: Add a dedicated 'Global-Fix' weekly rotation (owner: Eng-SRE, due 2026-02-01).
- A5: Run four 60-minute playbook drills (regional and cross-region scenarios) across Q1 2026 (owner: Eng-Platform, due 2026-04-30).

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Single roster source is a single point of configuration failure.
  - Mitigation: GitOps workflow with required PR approvals from two distinct oncall leads and automated unit tests for roster sanity (e.g., coverage by role, no overlapping primary slots).
- Risk: New rotation boundaries might reduce local oncall domain knowledge in small regional teams.
  - Mitigation: Pairing windows and weekly 'regional clinic' office hours during the first 8 weeks after rollout.

Dashboard and alert changes (examples):
- New dashboard panels: 'Active incident by rotation', 'Handoff count (last 24h)', 'Pages per oncaller (7d rolling)'.
- Alert label changes: add label rotation=americas|emea|apac. Use this label in the Alertmanager routing tree to control deduplication and notification channels.
- SLO watchlist: For the first 60 days after rollout, add SLOs for page-to-acknowledge 99th percentile to the daily ops digest.

Communication and rollout plan summary:
- Week 0 (pre-rollout): Publish runbook guidelines and hold two 1-hour training sessions.
- Week 1 (pilot): Enable merged rotations in PagerDuty for two non-critical services. Monitor for 7 days.
- Week 2–3: Iterate on config and runbooks based on pilot findings.
- Week 4 (full rollout): Switch remaining eligible services during low-traffic window and trigger verification playbooks.
- Week 5–12: Monitoring phase and weekly status updates to platform leadership.

Follow-ups and measurement plan:
- Weekly post-rollout review for first 8 weeks focusing on: handoff rate, paging noise, MTTA percentiles, pager overlap incidents.
- After 8 weeks produce an outcome memo with updated metrics and recommended further changes.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Project lead: Asha Patel (Eng-Platform)
- Infra-Automation: Ethan Morales
- Observability: Sofia Chen
- Eng-SRE liaison: Priya Nair
- Platform docs: Liam O'Connor
- Product stakeholder: Maya Rodriguez

Participants in retrospective workshop:
- 14 total: representatives from Platform (6), SRE (3), Infra (2), Product (2), Support (1).

Appendix — sample roster.yml schema (example snippet):

# roster.yml (example)
# Note: actual file is in infra/oncall/roster.yml in the platform repo
- rotation: americas-core
  primary: ["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com"]
  secondary: ["carol@example.com"]
  regions: ["us-central", "us-west"]

- rotation: emea-core
  primary: ["dan@example.com"]
  secondary: ["eve@example.com"]
  regions: ["eu-west-3", "eu-central-1"]

(Operational team: Do not edit roster.yml directly in PagerDuty. All changes must be PR -> CI -> PD-sync.)

Lessons learned (top three):
1. Simplify first, automate second: consolidations without automated, testable configuration caused the largest operational headaches.
2. Pilot in production at small scale is invaluable — it uncovered unexpected notification duplication caused by historic PD integrations.
3. Documentation and runbook normalization are as important as technical changes; consistent language reduced cognitive load during incidents.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should the Global-Fix rotation be staffed by a smaller, dedicated cross-functional team or a larger on-call pool? (Decision required by 2026-03-15).
- How should we handle customer-facing incident comms when multiple regions are involved? Propose a templated comms flow tied to rotation ownership.

Tags and archival notes:
- Retrospective created as part of continuous reliability improvements; archive after 18 months unless requirements change.
